store.1: I'm a fourth-year computer science major, and I'm 21, almost 22. My schedule can get hectic with classes and projects, but my hobbies help me stay sane. I love coding, and my outside interests give me a fresh perspective on programming. I believe taking breaks is important to avoid burnout. I also have a crush on someone in my advanced algorithms class. We were on the same team for a project and I really got to know her. She's funny and brilliant, and her sense of humor is up my alley. I'm trying to figure out how to work her into my day-to-day life with my chaotic schedule. She's also super dedicated to her studies, minoring in mathematics and having a passion for discrete structures. Our strengths complement each other well, as I'm more software-oriented and she's more math-oriented. We worked well together because she'd help me through complex analysis and combinatorial proofs. I trust her process, and we ended up getting an A on the project. I'm just happy for the chance to collaborate with her. The tricky part is figuring out if she's interested in me beyond just a team partner or classmate. I'm so busy with everything else—applications for full-time jobs, my internship from last summer wanting me to come back after graduation, and all my extracurriculars. I'm in the Robotics Club, which meets twice a week, and I'm also still involved in the sailing club. You know, I've been into sailing since I was a kid, so it's something I can't quite give up even when the semester is insane. Then there's the gym—remember, I try to work out every morning just to keep my sanity. The point is, I feel like I barely have enough hours in the day to keep up with all the responsibilities I already have. But when you really like someone, you can't help but want to carve out time for them, right?
